sections.name: File setup, out
sections.title: Setup and year range
sections.what: Sets the start year to 1980 and the end year to the current year, and prepares an empty table for the results.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The end year appears to keep the table current.
sections.watch_out: The end year comes from the computer clock, so two runs in different years give different tables.

sections.name: sources
sections.title: World Bank rates by economy
sections.what: Requests yearly official exchange rates for each mapped economy, in groups of twenty, keeping only positive values and recording where each series came from.
sections.why: Likely reason: the World Bank is the main source, and groups of twenty keep each request small.
sections.watch_out: An economy with no data is skipped with a warning, so its currency will not convert.

sections.name: twd
sections.title: Taiwan dollar rates from the Federal Reserve
sections.what: Downloads the Federal Reserve CSV for the Taiwan dollar and keeps the valid yearly values.
sections.why: The header says the World Bank does not publish a Taiwan dollar rate.
sections.watch_out: The script stops if no data comes back, and it assumes a fixed CSV layout.

sections.name: FX_TABLE
sections.title: Write the table file
sections.what: Writes the generated TypeScript file containing the rates, source notes, and the run date.
sections.why: The header says the table is written as a module so the server does not read files at run time.
sections.watch_out: The file is overwritten without a backup, so any hand edits are lost on the next run.

summary: A developer script that downloads yearly exchange rates from the World Bank and the US Federal Reserve, then rewrites the generated currency table the server uses to convert money into US dollars.
purpose: Keep the exchange rate table current so non-dollar money values convert correctly.
why: The header says the table is a generated module so that the bundled server carries the rates without reading a file at run time.
how: Lists each mapped economy and fetches yearly official exchange rates from the World Bank in groups of twenty. Keeps only positive values. Fetches Taiwan dollar rates from a Federal Reserve CSV file. Writes a TypeScript module holding the table, source notes, and the date of the run.
inputs: Economy mapping in src/lib/fx, the World Bank API, and the Federal Reserve CSV download.
outputs: Overwrites src/lib/fxTable.ts. Prints how many currencies were written.
risks: Overwrites a file marked 'do not edit by hand', so any local changes are lost. Any failed download stops the run. The end year comes from the computer's clock, so output changes depending on when it runs.
debug: If the World Bank returns an error code, the script stops and prints the address it tried. A currency with no data prints a warning and is left out. Check the date stamp at the top of the generated file to confirm when it was last built.
